This last .Rmd stage checks wolf ancestry from the Bayesian model results with similar standard methods as in Harmoinen et al. (2021) research paper, where i got my primer panel from. That is PCA, DAPC and NewHybrids.

## Libraries, settings, paths and basic setup

```{r setup}
suppressMessages({
  library(readxl)
  library(dplyr)
  library(readr)
  library(adegenet)
  library(tidyr)
})

# Settings from YAML header, turns them into usable variables
invisible(list2env(params, envir = environment()))

# Uploaded shared functions
source("Code/R_scripts/asp_functions.R", local = TRUE)
settings_used <- data.frame(setting = c("run_date", names(params)),
                            value = c(format(Sys.time(), "%Y-%m-%d %H:%M"),
                                      vapply(params, function(setting_value) paste(setting_value, collapse = ", "), character(1))))

# Paths for genotype and graphics outputs
graphics_dir <- file.path("Results", dataset_name, "Graphics")
genotypes_dir <- file.path("Results", dataset_name, "Genotypes_results")

# Shared function for building accurate settings based folder names
run_names <- build_run_names(input_type, use_anchors, anchor_length, threshold_type, error_rate, min_score_fraction,
                             prior_type, prior_het_share, prior_population, prior_floor, probe_type = probe_type,
                             ancestry_prior_shape = ancestry_prior_shape, phi_hom_structure = phi_hom_structure)# ancestry run
genotype_run_names <- build_run_names(input_type, use_anchors, anchor_length, threshold_type, error_rate, min_score_fraction,
                                      genotype_prior_type, prior_het_share, prior_population, prior_floor, probe_type = probe_type,
                                      ancestry_prior_shape = ancestry_prior_shape, phi_hom_structure = phi_hom_structure) #flat run
bayes_path <- file.path(genotypes_dir, genotype_run_names$bayes_run_name, "all_barcodes_base_mixture_genotypes_hierarchical.tsv") 
ref_path <- file.path("Data/Supporting_data/Reference_genotypes", paste0("genotypes_", dataset_name, ".tsv")) # Genotype references

# Separate output folder for real population setting
ancestry_out_dir <- file.path(graphics_dir, "STAN_Hierarchical", genotype_run_names$bayes_settings_label, paste0("Ancestry_validation_", reference_source))

dir.create(ancestry_out_dir, recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)

# Primer panel prep and importing for reference dogs and wolves
panel_sheet <- read_excel(primer_panel_path, sheet = "Final panel", .name_repair = "minimal")
panel_alleles <- data.frame(locus = panel_sheet[["SNP name"]],
                            allele1 = panel_sheet[["Allele 1"]],
                            allele2 = panel_sheet[["Allele 2"]],
                            wolf_frequency = as.numeric(panel_sheet[[match(wolf_frequency_column, names(panel_sheet))]]),
                            dog_frequency = as.numeric(panel_sheet[[match(dog_frequency_column, names(panel_sheet))]]))

# Imported shared data
bayes_raw <- read_tsv(bayes_path, show_col_types = FALSE)
stan <- bayes_raw %>%
  transmute(sample = barcode, locus, genotype = ifelse(GQ >= gq_cutoff, genotype_stan, NA), method = "Stan genotypes") # low GQ are saved as NA
naive <- bayes_raw %>%
  transmute(sample = barcode, locus, genotype = genotype_naive, method = "Naive genotypes")
ref <- read_tsv(ref_path, show_col_types = FALSE) %>%
  transmute(sample = sample_id, locus, genotype, method = "Reference genotypes")
stan_sample_parameters <- read_tsv(file.path(genotypes_dir, run_names$bayes_run_name, "sample_parameters_hierarchical.tsv"), show_col_types = FALSE) # wolf ancestry per sample from 05
```



## Which wolf allele frequencies fit the samples best
The original primer panel where I took my prior allele frequencies, primers and loci from, it also contains different columns for different freq of wolf sub populations in Europe. This chunk tests which column fits best for my set of wolves and hybrids. Chosen column (set of allele freq) specific to a sub population, is then used to simulate reference wolves, hybrids and dogs for later use in PCA, DAPC, NewHybirds.
Simulated reference wolves should resemble wolves in my study. It calculates how likely the observed genotypes of samples are under under HWE, column with the highest log likelihood fits the samples best. If i for example picked the Iberian population my "Dinaric" wolves would look more like hybrids than actual wolves.

```{r Wolf_Frequency_Fit}
# Grabs the the column that exst in the panel
wolf_frequency_columns <- intersect(c("FreqWOLF_all", "FreqWOLF_EastEurope", "FreqWOLF_IT", "FreqWOLF_IB"), names(panel_sheet))
# Only wolf-like samples are used (0.875 could have been set higher, this cutoff can be changed)
wolf_like_samples <- stan_sample_parameters$barcode[stan_sample_parameters$wolf_ancestry >= 0.875]

# Counts copies og allele 1 in each flat-prior Stan genotype from my samples which have GQ > 20 (filtered with NA not included)
wolf_like_genotypes <- stan %>%
  filter(sample %in% wolf_like_samples, !is.na(genotype)) %>%
  inner_join(panel_alleles[, c("locus", "allele1")], by = "locus") %>%
  mutate(allele1_copies = (substr(genotype, 1, 1) == allele1) + (substr(genotype, 2, 2) == allele1))

# Dataframe with one row per genotype sample locus pair and one colmn per population with allele 1 freq
column_frequencies <- sapply(wolf_frequency_columns, function(column_name)
  as.numeric(panel_sheet[[column_name]][match(wolf_like_genotypes$locus, panel_sheet[["SNP name"]])]))

# Only loci with complete set of frequencies
complete_rows <- complete.cases(column_frequencies)
# Settings floors so log doesnt produce infinity or 0 probability of a genotype
column_frequencies <- pmin(pmax(column_frequencies[complete_rows, , drop = FALSE], prior_floor), 1 - prior_floor)

# Prroduces HWE genotype probabiliity for every genotype with dbinom(copies, 2, p) = p^2, 2p(1 - p) or (1 - p)^2. East eruopean and FreqAll are almost as good meanwhile Iberian and Italian wolf popualtion clearly dont match. Based on  number of allele 1 copies of my stan flat prior it calculates log probabilites under each population, it adds them up.
wolf_frequency_fit <- data.frame(
  frequency_column = wolf_frequency_columns,
  log_likelihood = colSums(matrix(dbinom(wolf_like_genotypes$allele1_copies[complete_rows], 2, column_frequencies, log = TRUE), ncol = ncol(column_frequencies)))) %>%
  mutate(difference_to_best = log_likelihood - max(log_likelihood)) %>%
  arrange(desc(log_likelihood))

kable(wolf_frequency_fit, digits = 1, col.names = c("Wolf frequency column", "Log-likelihood", "Difference to best"))
```
  

## Reference animals, simulated hybrids, sample genotypes

```{r Reference_Animals}
### Data prep for PCA, combines reference, stan and naive genotypes in one table. It checks if the genotype is possible given the panel alleles of thatlocus. If its not it gives NA, wrong but possible calls stay in.
sample_genotypes <- bind_rows(ref, stan, naive) %>%
  inner_join(panel_alleles, by = "locus") %>%
  mutate(genotype = ifelse((substr(genotype, 1, 1) == allele1 | substr(genotype, 1, 1) == allele2) &
                             (substr(genotype, 2, 2) == allele1 | substr(genotype, 2, 2) == allele2), genotype, NA))

# My 33 loci with valid genotypes
pca_loci <- sort(unique(sample_genotypes$locus[!is.na(sample_genotypes$genotype)]))
# Panel rows in the same order as pca_loci
locus_alleles <- panel_alleles[match(pca_loci, panel_alleles$locus), ]
  
# How much the GQ filter removes
kable(summarise(sample_genotypes, Samples = n_distinct(sample), Genotypes = sum(!is.na(genotype)), Missing = sum(is.na(genotype)), .by = method), caption = sprintf("Genotypes per method over %d loci (Stan genotypes with GQ < %d set to missing)", length(pca_loci), gq_cutoff))

# Wide table one row per sample and method with loci as columns
sample_table <- sample_genotypes %>%
  transmute(individual = paste(sample, method, sep = " | "), group = method, locus, genotype) %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = locus, values_from = genotype)

### This part creates simulated reference animals (300 wolves and dogs with genotypes for 33 loci). They are generated from the primer panel frequencies, number of allele 1 copies is drawn from binomial distribution with 2 draws (HWE genotypes), which gets converted to genotypes and stored as geningd object fo adegenet. Further analysis need the reference points so that it can place my samples in space
set.seed(simulation_seed)

# Goes through all 33  frequencies, for each locus it draws 300 animals which gives 300  0,1,2 numbers per locus (600x33) or 186 animals for "real" setting.
if (reference_source == "real") {
  # Reads two real reference files from Harmoinen et al. (2021)
  reference_map <- read.table(reference_map_path, col.names = c("chromosome", "locus", "genetic_distance", "position"))
  reference_ped <- read.table(reference_ped_path, colClasses = "character") # as character becuase of "Ts"
  
  # Second column of the allele, skips first six columns and times two because each column hold info for for one allele
  allele_columns <- 6 + 2 * match(pca_loci, reference_map$locus)
  # Two tables for first and second allele for all 33 loci
  first_alleles <- as.matrix(reference_ped[, allele_columns - 1])
  second_alleles <- as.matrix(reference_ped[, allele_columns])
  real_allele1 <- matrix(rep(locus_alleles$allele1, each = nrow(reference_ped)), nrow = nrow(reference_ped))

  # Copies of allele 1 0, 1, 2 for HM, HT, or different HM, zero in the ped file is assigned to NA
  real_copies <- (first_alleles == real_allele1) + (second_alleles == real_allele1)
  real_copies[first_alleles == "0" | second_alleles == "0"] <- NA

  # Sample draws n_reference_woolves amount of random animals from the assigned groups in settings
  wolf_rows <- sample(which(reference_ped$V1 %in% reference_wolf_groups), n_reference_wolves)
  dog_rows <- sample(which(reference_ped$V1 %in% reference_dog_groups), n_reference_dogs)
  parent_copies <- real_copies[c(wolf_rows, dog_rows), ]
} else {
  parent_copies <- rbind(sapply(locus_alleles$wolf_frequency, function(frequency) rbinom(n_reference_wolves, 2, frequency)),
                         sapply(locus_alleles$dog_frequency, function(frequency) rbinom(n_reference_dogs, 2, frequency)))
}

# Label for each row
parent_group <- rep(c("Simulated wolf", "Simulated dog"), c(n_reference_wolves, n_reference_dogs))

# Allele 1 and 2  letters for each locus repetead for every animal
allele1_matrix <- matrix(rep(locus_alleles$allele1, each = nrow(parent_copies)), nrow = nrow(parent_copies))
allele2_matrix <- matrix(rep(locus_alleles$allele2, each = nrow(parent_copies)), nrow = nrow(parent_copies))

# Based on a number 0, 1, 2 it becomes a genotype and gets the alleles form previous matrices
parent_genotypes <- ifelse(parent_copies == 2, paste0(allele1_matrix, allele1_matrix),
                           ifelse(parent_copies == 1, paste0(allele1_matrix, allele2_matrix), paste0(allele2_matrix, allele2_matrix)))
colnames(parent_genotypes) <- pca_loci
parent_genotypes[is.na(parent_genotypes)] <- "" # missing genotypes for real animals from reference population

# Turns it into a genind object, each allele is one character with names and parent groups
parent_genind <- df2genind(as.data.frame(parent_genotypes), ncode = 1, ploidy = 2,
                           ind.names = paste(parent_group, seq_along(parent_group)), pop = parent_group, NA.char = "")

#These are split using pop for later hybridize() which need two parent populations (for backcrosses)
wolf_genind <- parent_genind[pop(parent_genind) == "Simulated wolf"]
dog_genind <- parent_genind[pop(parent_genind) == "Simulated dog"]

### This part creates simulated hybrids from the simulated wolves and dogs and turns my samples into genind objects as well and combines everything into one complete genind that feeds the PCA and DAPC
# All the possible hybridizations with second backcrosses as well.
f1_genind <- hybridize(wolf_genind, dog_genind, n = n_simulated_per_hybrid_class, pop = "Simulated F1", hyb.label = "F1_", quiet = TRUE) #  50 %
backcross_wolf_genind <- hybridize(wolf_genind, f1_genind, n = n_simulated_per_hybrid_class, pop = "Simulated backcross to wolf", hyb.label = "BCwolf_", quiet = TRUE) # 75 %
backcross_dog_genind <- hybridize(dog_genind, f1_genind, n = n_simulated_per_hybrid_class, pop = "Simulated backcross to dog", hyb.label = "BCdog_", quiet = TRUE) # 25 %
second_backcross_wolf_genind <- hybridize(wolf_genind, backcross_wolf_genind, n = n_simulated_per_hybrid_class, pop = "Simulated second backcross to wolf", hyb.label = "BC2wolf_", quiet = TRUE) # 87.5 %
second_backcross_dog_genind <- hybridize(dog_genind, backcross_dog_genind, n = n_simulated_per_hybrid_class, pop = "Simulated second backcross to dog", hyb.label = "BC2dog_", quiet = TRUE)  # 12.5%

# Locus column in pca_loci order
genotype_columns <- as.data.frame(sample_table[, pca_loci])
genotype_columns[is.na(genotype_columns)] <- "" # replaces NA for "" for genind

# Genind for my samples, pop is set by group (stan, naive, reference)
sample_genind <- df2genind(genotype_columns, ncode = 1, ploidy = 2, ind.names = sample_table$individual, pop = sample_table$group, NA.char = "")

# Combines all either 2172 animals with simulatede setting (300 per group) or 1374 with real setting (186 per group)
all_genind <- repool(parent_genind, f1_genind, backcross_wolf_genind, backcross_dog_genind,
                     second_backcross_wolf_genind, second_backcross_dog_genind, sample_genind)
animal_group <- as.character(pop(all_genind))

# Saves .rds for the plotting stage
saveRDS(list(all_genind = all_genind, animal_group = animal_group, parent_copies = parent_copies, pca_loci = pca_loci),
           file.path(ancestry_out_dir, "ancestry_inputs.rds"))
```



## NewHybrids input data preparation
This chunk contains data prep for NewHybrids software with correct genotype codes per sample. It computes posterior probability for all six classes with Harmoinen et al (2021) research paper in mind. 100 simulated wolves and dogs are inputed as known pure parents (z0 for wolves, z1 for dogs). My samples use the flat prior as previious PCA analysis with same GQ cutoff.

Command used to run NewHybrids from the folder: 
`~/Tools/newhybrids/bin/OSX/newhybsng -d newhybrids_input.txt --burn-in 100000`
`--num-sweeps 500000 --theta-prior Jeffreys --pi-prior Jeffreys -s 1 2 --no-gui`

```{r NewHybrids_Input}
# Number of simulated wolves and dogs as pure parents, reference point for NewHybrids
n_newhybrids_reference <- 100 

# New folder for NewHybrids inside ancestry analysis
newhybrids_dir <- file.path(ancestry_out_dir, "NewHybrids")
dir.create(newhybrids_dir, showWarnings = FALSE)

# Takes the wide sample table wtih sample rows by method and column as loci. stan genotypes used only in pca_loci order and turns it into matrix
stan_genotype_letters <- as.matrix(sample_table[sample_table$group == "Stan genotypes", pca_loci])

# Count copies of allele 1 and write the number insdie each cell (0, 1, 2) with the help of allele1_letters. Same trick as before.
allele1_letters <- matrix(rep(locus_alleles$allele1, each = nrow(stan_genotype_letters)), nrow = nrow(stan_genotype_letters))
sample_copies <- (substr(stan_genotype_letters, 1, 1) == allele1_letters) + (substr(stan_genotype_letters, 2, 2) == allele1_letters)

# Picks 100 refeerence animals from previously made 300 parent copies (wolves 1 -300, 301- 600 dogs ) and stack them
reference_copies <- parent_copies[c(1:n_newhybrids_reference, n_reference_wolves + 1:n_newhybrids_reference), ]
newhybrids_copies <- rbind(reference_copies, sample_copies)

# Turns the 0, 1, 2 number into NewHyibrids input codes.
newhybrids_genotypes <- ifelse(is.na(newhybrids_copies), "0", c("22", "12", "11")[newhybrids_copies + 1])
# Adds flags, z0 for known pure animal from popualtion 0 (wolf), z1 for pure dogs, "" unkown, what the software estimates
newhybrids_flags <- c(rep("z0", n_newhybrids_reference), rep("z1", n_newhybrids_reference), rep("", nrow(sample_copies)))
newhybrids_lines <- paste(seq_len(nrow(newhybrids_genotypes)), newhybrids_flags, apply(newhybrids_genotypes, 1, paste, collapse = " "))

# writes the file for NewHybrids
writeLines(c(paste("NumIndivs", nrow(newhybrids_genotypes)), paste("NumLoci", length(pca_loci)), "Digits 1", "Format Lumped", "",
             paste("LocusNames", paste(pca_loci, collapse = " ")), "", newhybrids_lines),
           file.path(newhybrids_dir, "newhybrids_input.txt"))

# Key to match the NewHybrids output rows back to the animals
newhybrids_key <- data.frame(index = seq_len(nrow(newhybrids_genotypes)), animal = c(paste("Simulated wolf", 1:n_newhybrids_reference), paste("Simulated dog", 1:n_newhybrids_reference), sub(" \\| .*", "", sample_table$individual[sample_table$group == "Stan genotypes"])),flag = newhybrids_flags)

write_tsv(newhybrids_key, file.path(newhybrids_dir, "newhybrids_key.tsv"))
```



## NewHybrids power input data preparation
This part checks how sure you can be that the NewHybirds classification is correct, it test how much you can trust each class from my 24 samples. Same idea as in the Harmoinen et al. research paper. It saves into a separete folder, it tests 100 animals per 5 hybrid classes.

```{r NewHybrids_Power_Input}
# simulated hybrids per class as in referencer research paper
n_power_per_class <- 100 
power_classes <- c("Simulated F1", "Simulated backcross to wolf", "Simulated backcross to dog",
                   "Simulated second backcross to wolf", "Simulated second backcross to dog")
# Output path
newhybrids_power_dir <- file.path(ancestry_out_dir, "NewHybrids_power")
dir.create(newhybrids_power_dir, showWarnings = FALSE)

# First 100 animals of every simulated hybrid class, copies of allele 1 read from the genind
power_rows <- unlist(lapply(power_classes, function(group_name) which(animal_group == group_name)[1:n_power_per_class]))
# Safety check my first run ran with only 50 animals accidentaly
stopifnot(!anyNA(power_rows))
power_copies <- tab(all_genind[power_rows])[, paste0(pca_loci, ".", locus_alleles$allele1)]


# Same reference wolves (z0) and dogs (z1) as in the previous run, same file prep
power_input_copies <- rbind(reference_copies, power_copies)
power_genotypes <- ifelse(is.na(power_input_copies), "0", c("22", "12", "11")[power_input_copies + 1])
power_flags <- c(rep("z0", n_newhybrids_reference), rep("z1", n_newhybrids_reference), rep("", nrow(power_copies)))
power_lines <- paste(seq_len(nrow(power_genotypes)), power_flags, apply(power_genotypes, 1, paste, collapse = " "))

writeLines(c(paste("NumIndivs", nrow(power_genotypes)), paste("NumLoci", length(pca_loci)), "Digits 1", "Format Lumped", "",
             paste("LocusNames", paste(pca_loci, collapse = " ")), "", power_lines),
           file.path(newhybrids_power_dir, "newhybrids_power_input.txt"))

# Key with the true class of every animal
power_key <- data.frame(index = seq_len(nrow(power_genotypes)),
                        true_class = c(rep("Simulated wolf", n_newhybrids_reference),
                                       rep("Simulated dog", n_newhybrids_reference), animal_group[power_rows]),
                        flag = power_flags)
write_tsv(power_key, file.path(newhybrids_power_dir, "newhybrids_power_key.tsv"))
```



## STRUCTURE input data preparation
This chunk contains input data prep for STRUCTURE analysis. Specific allele strucutre input for all 33 loci and mainparams and extraparams file with mainly defualt values except for settings which are relavant to analysis from Harmoinen et al. Run with admixutre model, correlated allele freq, 50000 burn in and 500000 repetitions, and 95 % interval (ANCESTPINT) so its later comparable to my Bayesian ancestry run, two clusters (k = 2, for wolf and dog) with fixed seed.

Command for running STRUCTURE:

`for run in 1 2 3 4 5; do`
 `~/Tools/structure/structure_kernel_src/structure -m mainparams -e extraparams`
 `-K 2 -D $run -o structure_K2_run$run > log_run$run.txt &`
 `done; wait`

```{r STRUCTURE_Input}
# New output paths for STRUCTURE
structure_dir <- file.path(ancestry_out_dir, "STRUCTURE")
dir.create(structure_dir, showWarnings = FALSE)

# All the parent animals and samples combined (186 reference wolves and dogs and 24 samples)
structure_copies <- rbind(parent_copies, sample_copies)
# Makes names for reference animals wolf_1 to wolf_186 and so on, my samples keep id
structure_labels <- c(paste0("wolf_", seq_len(n_reference_wolves)), paste0("dog_", seq_len(n_reference_dogs)), newhybrids_key$animal[newhybrids_key$flag == ""])
# Makes 1 (wolf), 2 (dog), 3 (sample) labels for STR  
structure_population <- rep(1:3, c(n_reference_wolves, n_reference_dogs, nrow(sample_copies)))

# Converts it into allele input type for STRUCTURE (if to copies of allele 1, then its converted to 1 meaning HM for allele 1)
first_allele <- ifelse(is.na(structure_copies), -9, ifelse(structure_copies >= 1, 1, 2))
second_allele <- ifelse(is.na(structure_copies), -9, ifelse(structure_copies == 2, 1, 2))

# Binds two column for both alleles per locus in pca_loci order
structure_alleles <- cbind(first_allele, second_allele)[, order(rep(seq_along(pca_loci), 2))]

# writes input file for STRUCTURE with header names
writeLines(c(paste(pca_loci, collapse = " "), paste(structure_labels, structure_population, apply(structure_alleles, 1, paste, collapse = " "))), file.path(structure_dir, "structure_input.txt"))

# Same settings as in Harmoinen et al. run with admixutre model, correlated allele freq, 50000 burn in and 500000 repetitions, and 95 % interval (ANCESTPINT) so its later comparable to my Bayesian ancestry run, two clusters (k = 2, for wolf and dog) with fixed seed. All other param are mainly defualts.
structure_mainparams <- c(MAXPOPS = "2", BURNIN = "50000", NUMREPS = "500000", INFILE = "structure_input.txt", 
                          OUTFILE = "structure_output", NUMINDS = nrow(structure_alleles), NUMLOCI = length(pca_loci), 
                          PLOIDY = "2", MISSING = "-9", ONEROWPERIND = "1", LABEL = "1", POPDATA = "1", POPFLAG = "0", 
                          LOCDATA = "0", PHENOTYPE = "0", EXTRACOLS = "0", MARKERNAMES = "1", RECESSIVEALLELES = "0", 
                          MAPDISTANCES = "0", PHASED = "0", PHASEINFO = "0", MARKOVPHASE = "0", NOTAMBIGUOUS = "-999")

structure_extraparams <- c(NOADMIX = "0", LINKAGE = "0", USEPOPINFO = "0", LOCPRIOR = "0", FREQSCORR = "1", ONEFST = "0", 
                           INFERALPHA = "1", POPALPHAS = "0", ALPHA = "1.0", INFERLAMBDA = "0", POPSPECIFICLAMBDA = "0",
```
